fields.h1: Build a Talent Show Sign-Up Sheet That Sets the Lineup

fields.explore_cta: Build My Talent Show Sign-Up Sheet
fields.features_heading: What the Sheet Sorts Out Before Rehearsal
fields.features_subheading: A talent show sign up sheet settles who performs, for how long, and in what order. Describe your show, and Emergent builds it.
fields.feature_1:
One question per screen on a phone

Asks a performer one thing at a time, from the act name to the minutes it runs. A parent filling it in at pickup or a student between classes never has to squint at a crowded grid.
fields.feature_2:
A time limit the sheet enforces

Checks each act's length against the limit you set for the show. An entry over the limit goes back to the performer with the cap shown, before the act can join the lineup.
fields.feature_3:
Groups entered once, with every name

Lets a band or dance crew sign up as one act and list every member and grade. Each name is counted toward that student's total, so a cap on acts per student holds for groups too.
fields.feature_4:
Stage needs and tracks on the entry

Asks how many mics an act needs, whether it uses the piano, and for its backing track as a file. The stage crew works from one cue sheet, not a pile of notes and texts.
fields.feature_5:
A running order you can rearrange

Turns the sign-ups into a numbered lineup with each act's length and running total. Set a rule such as no two songs in a row, and the order follows it as new acts sign up.
fields.feature_6:
Code that leaves with you

Exports the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A school district or a theater can host the sheet on its own servers and reuse it for every season's show.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a talent show sign up sheet for my school's spring show where each act enters its name, length, and stage needs.

faq_plan.q: What is a talent show sign up sheet?
How do I create a talent show sign up sheet?

plan.angle: The top 10 for talent show sign up sheet is printables (Etsy, Twinkl, Scribd, a PDF to pin on the office door) and generic registration templates (Jotform, Cognito, FormNX): a grid of names and acts that the organizer then turns into a running order by hand. This page shows the sheet as a phone form that does the organizer's sorting: an elementary PTA show that holds every act to 3 minutes, a high school show where no student appears in more than 2 acts, a community fundraiser where piano and mic requests reach the stage manager before rehearsal, and a workplace charity show whose running order keeps 2 singing acts apart. The FAQ covers what to ask, act length, group acts, running order, closing dates, workplace shows and what to keep off the sheet.
tab_stories: At Maplewick Elementary, PTA chair Orsolya Trelawney holds every act to 3 minutes, so when a parent enters 4 minutes for Cazimir Wetherell's yo-yo routine, the form asks for 3 minutes or less before it saves; 22 acts are signed up.

At Coldharbour High, drama teacher Isolde Moncrieff allows each student 2 acts, so when the Velvet Static dance crew lists Ravi Galloway-Shin, who is already in 2 acts, the crew's entry waits on Isolde's review list.

At the Quarrington Community Theater fundraiser, every act lists its mics and uploads a backing track, and when Teodor Blackwood asks for the piano, the app emails stage manager Solveig Marchbanks; 14 of 16 tracks are in.

At the Wetherby Packaging charity show, emcee Ingeborg Vasquez gets a running order of 12 acts that never puts 2 singing acts back to back, so Ines Abernathy's song moves from slot 5 to slot 6, after a comedy act.
